result.text: The sales clerks in a bank can use their software frontend to receive the credit-scoring for a certain customer.
This starts a process in the banking system which communicates with the agency in the background.
This process sends a scoring request to the agency right after the beginning.
Then, the Agency does a first quick scoring (level 1).
This will often lead to an immediate result which is then returned directly to the banking system within seconds.
The banking process presents the result to the clerk sitting at the frontend.
Sometimes the scoring cannot be determined immediately and takes longer.
In this case the agency informs the banking process of the delay and then starts the level 2 scoring (which can take up to a couple of minutes).
After the scoring result is determined, the information is sent back to the banking process.
The banking process displays a message to the clerk when he receives information about the delay to check again later.
As soon as the result arrives, it can be seen at the frontend.

result.process_description:
The sales clerks in a bank can use their software frontend to receive the credit-scoring for a certain customer. 
This starts a process in the banking system which communicates with the agency in the background. 
This process sends a scoring request to the agency right after the beginning. 
Then, the Agency does a first quick scoring (level 1). 
This will often lead to an immediate result which is then returned directly to the banking system within seconds. 
The banking process presents the result to the clerk sitting at the frontend. 
Sometimes the scoring cannot be determined immediately and takes longer. 
In this case the agency informs the banking process of the delay and then starts the level 2 scoring (which can take up to a couple of minutes). 
After the scoring result is determined, the information is sent back to the banking process. 
The banking process displays a message to the clerk when he receives information about the delay to check again later. 
As soon as the result arrives, it can be seen at the frontend.

result.rule: Do not create separate pools for ordinary internal roles unless the description treats them as independent communicating participants.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
Use sequence flows inside one participant process and message flows between different participants. Never use sequence flow across pools.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.

result.rule: When the description says a person uses a software application to send requests to and receive results from a process running in another system, so the application itself exchanges messages with that process: Model the software application as its own pool, separate from any pool representing the human user. Connect the application pool to the process pool with message flows: one from the application pool to the process's message start event, one from the process's sending task to the application pool, and one from the process's sending task to a catch event in the process pool that waits for the reply. Do not let the human user's pool or a task in the process stand in for the application as the message sender.

When the description states that an external participant initiates a process by sending it a message, and that the process in turn sends a message to a further independent participant that responds with messages in both directions: Model each independent participant as its own pool. Model the process's start as a message start event in the process pool, and connect the initiating participant's sending node in its own pool to that start event with a message flow. Connect each outgoing message from the process to a receiving node inside the other participant's pool, and connect each response back to a catch event or receive task in the process pool. Keep any processing steps that the independent participant performs inside its own pool. Never attach a message flow to a pool boundary.

When the description says the process sends a request or case to an external party and then only waits for that party's outcome or a deadline, without describing any step the external party itself performs: Model the send as a task in the process's own pool, and model the awaited outcome as intermediate catch events or an event-based gateway in that same pool. Do not create a separate pool for the external party, and do not add message flows to or from it, unless the description states that the party performs process steps or communicates as an independent participant.

When the description states that a process begins through one of several alternative channels joined by 'or', so that each channel is a separate way to start the same case: Model a single start event followed by an exclusive gateway. Give that gateway one outgoing flow to a task for each alternative channel, and join the channel tasks with an exclusive merge gateway placed before the first common step. Do not attach the channel tasks directly to the start event or leave them unconnected to a decision.
